diagnosis.mechanism: At Hardbruecke the messages increased the alighting score and lowered the continuation score, changing alight to continue. The public arm then transferred at HB to S5; the own/local arm waited at Hardbruecke for S11 and arrived 343 seconds earlier.
diagnosis.interpretation: The relevant S11/S5 predictions were received 476 seconds before the first fork. This is a stale-snapshot exposure, not proof that forecast age caused the loss. The scores also integrate service uncertainty, the frozen trip law, and surrogate tail values.

diagnosis.mechanism: At HB both arms saw S7 departure 231 at 30011 with the same visit history. Messages raised the wait score for S14 227 from 30646.177 to 31207.792, so the public arm boarded S7. The own/local arm waited six more seconds for S14 and arrived 885 seconds earlier.
diagnosis.interpretation: The S14 departure prediction was 30000, received at 30003 and used at 30011; the realized departure was 30017. A 17-second endpoint forecast error alone does not explain the 561.615-second change in expected wait score. The fixed likelihood, discretized joint trip posterior, no-offer risk and downstream scoring all enter that score.

diagnosis.mechanism: At Oerlikon both absolute scores improved after messages, but continuation improved more: the public arm continued by a 5.371-second modeled margin, while own/local alighted by 53.359 seconds. Public continued to HB and boarded S12; own/local used S16 from Oerlikon and arrived 259 seconds earlier.
diagnosis.interpretation: The highlighted forecasts were 157 seconds old. This is a near-boundary decision in the declared model, with a negative realized outcome; a single realized world does not establish that the expected-value ranking was mathematically wrong.

findings: All three combined-control first forks have identical hard own/local history and available message receipts only. No nonoperating notice is active at any first fork. Received numerical forecasts change the declared conditional scores and action boundary. No implementation error is established by these three negative realized outcomes.
limitations: The arm comparison identifies the effect of the complete message-processing/control bundle in these fixed realized worlds. Later histories and message use also diverge, so total loss is not an isolated causal effect of the first changed action or a single forecast. Forecast-error calibration, posterior discretization, frozen-snapshot tail surrogates and future revisions are not separated by this audit. Dates are development data, not confirmation.
selection: Inherited selection_uses_actual:false metadata has been corrected. Static menus do not use actuals; final eligibility uses actual coverage/consistency and message timing, never forecast values or policy loss.
